summary: Reserve, Stalwart, Discipline keywords, and a new Removed-from-Game zone (issue #184). Zone.RemovedFromGame + RemoveFromGame(card) + PlayerView.RemovedFromGame (visible like the existing discard piles). Discipline: new Timing 'Discipline', playable from a discard pile, cost = the card's own printed GoldCost, removed from the game after resolving -- reuses the existing per-instance AbilityUses dedupe for free. Stalwart: new StalwartNegatesBow(card, actingPlayerId), retrofitted onto every existing ability that bows a chosen target (~12 call sites) -- never the card's own controller. Reserve: a new recruitReserve command (Dynasty side, an absent battle action recruiting straight to the battlefield, skipping assignment) and equip-battle's Target generalized from Spell-only to any Item/Follower/Spell carrying Reserve (Fate side), withholding the bonus Additional Action grant for non-Spells. First real cards: Hida Kurabi, Matsu Ryohei, Shiba Jikaro (Personality Wave 6), Floating Reserve (Follower Wave 6) -- all pure reminder text. Nine more Reserve cards found in the same audit are deferred with documented blockers.
validation: dotnet build clean (L5R.Core + L5R.Client, catching a real client-side PlayerView constructor break in TabletopProbe.cs, now fixed); full test suite 110/110 core + 34/34 published + 8/8 deck-format; bash tools/check.sh --skip-client all green (13/13 AI, 5/5 server integration, 4/4 client transport integration).
remaining: Nine deferred Reserve cards each need something else first (Absent Interrupt, Absent Engage, a Spells-in-unit Attack axis, conditional cost reduction, an action-redirect mechanic, or Ring-timing clarification) -- see docs/CARD_INVENTORY.xlsx Blocker notes. No client UI exists yet for the Removed-from-Game pile -- explicitly Alfredo's own follow-up per the user's spec. The Attack-deferral path correctly carries the Additional-Action flag across an entry-reaction window that opens mid-resolution, but that specific interaction (dangling grant + entry-reaction window in the same action) is a narrow, pre-existing gap from #181, not newly introduced here.
